summary: Scores: D1 experience 7.5, D2 engineering 8.5, D3 content 8.0. The merged spec takes D1's IA and flows (fifth Prayer tab, flat query-param routes, permission at point of use, stub-and-slot pattern, calm rules), D2's engineering seams (isAppRoute and five-point sync registration, notification ID registry with the iOS 64 budget, hash-skipped rescheduling, single native writer compile-checked on a mobile/ branch, licence fragments, bundle check, ids lock) and D3's content pipeline (one file per item, two-witness collation, attributed gradings, positions as data, staged fresh-agent checks, 15 build-enforced guardrails). Key conflict resolutions: the prayer engine and Hijri conversion are fully implemented in foundations so most packages build in wave 1; D2's bundled hadith-api Arabic is rejected in favour of D3's witness collation, with a skeleton-hash check added; place, prayer settings, worship logs and zakat are device-only (place also excluded from backup), only the learning store syncs; emitted content is per deck so nothing emitted is shared; course ships Purification and Fasting now, Prayer unit deferred. Plan: 1 foundations package, 10 wave-1 packages, 6 wave-2 packages, 2 wave-3 packages (content audit, integration). Verified in the repo: working tree is clean on main, REMINDER_ID_BASE is 7100, the manifest strips SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM, applySm2 is private, android.yml runs on mobile/** pushes. Flags for the owner: the exact-alarm manifest change reverses an earlier decision; android-native needs a push to a mobile/** branch for its compile check; content agents need web access for witnesses and will ship fewer items than authored if witnesses are unreachable; all religious content ships labelled as not yet scholar-reviewed.

Intro card (deck metadata) states honestly: the sound hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim says Allah has ninety-nine names and does not list them; the familiar list comes through al-Tirmidhi's narration, which he calls gharib and which many hadith scholars (e.g. Ibn Hajar, Ibn Kathir) hold to be a narrator's addition; the deck teaches it as the widely known enumeration. Confirm each of these citations in two sources before writing a number; otherwise cite by collection and book without a number.

touchesShared: replaces foundations stub src/content/deen/decks/course-purification.ts; new works/scholars via registry-additions.json sidecar only
packages.brief:
Read .claude/CLAUDE.md and .claude/plans/allinone-spec.md (section 5 in full, plus 1, 9, 12) and content/deen/STYLE.md. Content only: you write lesson JSON (Lesson/Claim types in src/types/deen.ts) validated by node scripts/build-deen.mjs --deck course-purification; the UI is built by another package. Do not edit files in spec 3.8.

Write Unit Purification as about 9 micro-lessons (about 2 minutes each, at most 6 claims) in content/deen/course/purification/lessons/: why purity and the kinds of water; wudu step by step; the obligatory acts of wudu (schools differ on intention, order, continuity, rubbing, how much of the head); what breaks wudu (agreed items, then the differences: touching the opposite sex, touching the private part, bleeding, sleep); ghusl; tayammum; wiping over leather socks; removing impurity; recap. Plus unit.json and ids.lock.json.

Grounding rules (hard): every claim has evidence: a Quran ref (verify the ayah in src/data/surah-*.json), a hadith given as a full Citation you have confirmed in two witnesses (if the hadith is not already a corpus item, add it as a TextItem under content/deen/course/purification/evidence/ following the same witness rules, or cite Quran/consensus instead), or a consensus citation by work and chapter (Ibn al-Mundhir's al-Ijma', Ibn Hazm's Maratib al-Ijma', or Ibn Rushd reporting agreement). Claims of kind 'differs' carry positions for the schools from the fixed primers — Hanafi: Mukhtasar al-Quduri; Maliki: al-Risala of Ibn Abi Zayd; Shafi'i: Matn Abi Shuja'; Hanbali: 'Umdat al-Fiqh — cited by work and chapter (kitab/bab) with the Arabic phrase relied on stored in quote, located in an online copy of the primer (web fetch), and each difference cross-located in Ibn Rushd's Bidayat al-Mujtahid. No tarjih: never 'the correct opinion', 'the strongest view', or 'scholars agree' without a consensus citation. No ruling without a source; a claim you cannot source is cut, not softened. Lesson intro at most 60 words with no ruling vocabulary. Each claim has 1-2 authored recall cards; each lesson 2-4 check questions tied to a claim. Arabic terms in English are written [[term-id]] and defined in content/deen/glossary/course-purification.json (own definitions). A fresh checker pass (separate sub-agent that did not draft) re-locates every primer quote and evidence citation and logs findings in review.log; lessons that fail stay draft and are not emitted.

Finish: run the build for the deck, commit emitted files, set the deck module ready:true only if at least 5 lessons are source-checked, add the licence fragment (own work; primers and classical works are public domain, cited not reproduced). Acceptance: build-deen --check green (guardrails 10-15), vitest and tsc green; report lesson counts shipped vs draft and list every primer citation you could not confirm. Do not push.
